Unitree G1 vs Booster K1

Humanoid robot comparison · 2026

The Unitree G1 and Booster K1 are two humanoid robots aimed at different markets. The G1 is a more general-purpose humanoid development platform, while the K1 is focused more on education, research, interaction, and robotics development.

The important distinction is whether you want a robot for advanced physical manipulation and locomotion or a platform for accessible humanoid robotics development.

1. Specifications side by side

*The G1's advertised maximum speed should not be confused with sustained walking speed. Specifications and runtime depend on configuration.

2. Where the G1 is better

The G1 has several advantages:

Physical capabilities: Larger actuators and higher joint torque, particularly useful for dynamic movement.

Mobility: More mature dynamic locomotion capabilities.

Size: Its 132 cm height makes it more representative of a human-sized working robot.

Manipulation: EDU configurations can support sophisticated three-finger hands.

Perception: Depth camera and 3D LiDAR provide a stronger sensor combination.

The G1 EDU is particularly interesting for research involving reinforcement learning, imitation learning, whole-body control and manipulation.

One important warning: the inexpensive G1 Base is not equivalent to the G1 EDU. The latter is the more appropriate development platform.

3. Where the Booster K1 is better

The K1 has some compelling advantages:

Lower weight: At 19.5 kg, it is considerably easier to transport.

Lower entry price: Particularly attractive for educational institutions and robotics labs.

AI compute: Different editions offer up to 200 TOPS.

ROS 2 development: Designed with robotics education and development in mind.

Practical deployment: Its smaller dimensions make it easier to use in classrooms, demonstrations and controlled research environments.

The K1 is especially interesting for multi-robot experiments, robotics education, AI perception and humanoid soccer research.

My verdict

Choose Unitree G1 EDU if:

You want a more capable physical humanoid, advanced locomotion, manipulation research and sophisticated whole-body control.

Choose Booster K1 if:

You want an affordable, lightweight development platform for AI, ROS 2, education, experimentation and multiple-robot projects.

My preference: G1 EDU for serious humanoid robotics research. K1 for a lower-cost development and experimentation platform.

One question that would change my recommendation

What is your primary objective?

A. AI development – LLMs, vision, autonomous decision-making.

B. Robotics research – ROS 2, reinforcement learning, motion planning.

C. Physical capabilities – walking, running, dancing, manipulation.

D. Commercial use – demonstrations, reception, interaction.

E. Research platform – developing your own humanoid software and control algorithms.

I can then compare the exact G1 and K1 editions, including onboard computing, SDK access, ROS 2 support, upgrade options and actual performance, rather than just comparing their marketing specifications.
